method: Assistant source-derived checklist prepared without reading current target outputs; no human labels and no additional target calls. These 24 relations are an explicit audit set, not exhaustive human-gold correctness labels. Do not feed it to the generation context.

checks.expected_relation: Preserve analyze, saved JSON read and markdown summary write. A specific returned save filepath can identify a write; list/latest examples select stored files and do not themselves prove membership in the current analysis.
checks.incorrect_or_unestablished_claim: An analysis-to-read control edge, category, filename timestamp or operation label proves that the read consumes this exact current result.

checks.expected_relation: Keep module import and dotenv config side effect distinct. Both index and direct API imports can reach settings through imports; neither calls every exported API function merely by loading the module.
checks.incorrect_or_unestablished_claim: Index reexports execute all functions; direct API import bypasses settings initialization; unknown dotenv effects are no-op.

checks.expected_relation: Retain declared .env creation and installation as workflow side effects, then environment values including private key newline normalization, service account email, property, site and date default. The credentials in SKILL are examples/placeholders, not actual secrets.
checks.incorrect_or_unestablished_claim: Invent actual credentials or treat the declaration/example as evidence that a concrete credential file was already created or sent.

checks.expected_relation: Validation checks presence and names missing settings. Constructors consume client_email/private_key and auth scopes, with opaque SDK internal behavior. Both webmasters.readonly and indexing scopes enter the shared GoogleAuth constructor.
checks.incorrect_or_unestablished_claim: Validation error strings contain secret key plaintext; every eventual API request transmits the private key plaintext; the handle is itself credential plaintext.

checks.expected_relation: Three independently cached clients return existing handles on cache hits; otherwise validate, construct and assign. Preserve credential provenance at creation and distinguish future reset/creation. Reset does not erase historical calls.
checks.incorrect_or_unestablished_claim: Each getClient necessarily reloads or creates a handle; every cached client necessarily uses the newest environment; reset retracts old exposures.

checks.expected_relation: Only absent/falsy date input reads settings default. Object input is returned directly. Shorthand conversion differs for Search Console ISO dates versus GA4 relative dates; invalid strings fall back to 30 days.
checks.incorrect_or_unestablished_claim: A legal object-return branch requires a fake compute or model-observation boundary; runtime arguments/defaults may be silently discarded.

checks.topic: Standard report request identity and ignored options
checks.expected_relation: Request contains property/dateRanges/mapped dimension and metric names plus truthy limit. filters and orderBy are documented/destructured but are not placed into the request. Returned first response is unchanged except the TypeScript cast.
checks.incorrect_or_unestablished_claim: Claim filters/orderBy execute, claim casts select only declared fields, or certify intended filter constraints are met.

checks.expected_relation: Keep four call sites and each dimension/metric pair; retain save flags and original response versions. Live snapshot invokes only three of these helpers.
checks.incorrect_or_unestablished_claim: Merge all four request/response pairs into one response identity; firstUserSource data is necessarily requested by liveSnapshot.

checks.expected_relation: Dimensions-only and metrics-only helpers select the corresponding array after whole acquisition. getPropertyMetadata saves and returns the full response; getAvailableFields returns full metadata even though console output only logs two counts.
checks.incorrect_or_unestablished_claim: Count logging narrows getAvailableFields return to counts; whole full-metadata output is inherently unnecessary; property metadata necessarily contains raw user data.

checks.topic: Search Console recipient payload and one offset
checks.expected_relation: Preserve siteUrl receiver context and request body dates/dimensions/rowLimit/startRow. response.data is selected from the SDK envelope; row contents remain intact. One offset-bearing request is not a pagination loop.
checks.incorrect_or_unestablished_claim: Treat HTTP headers/envelope as returned payload; invent repeated pagination until exhaustion.

checks.expected_relation: URL_UPDATED and URL_DELETED are separate typed requests. The returned URL is response metadata URL if truthy, otherwise input URL; notifyTime uses response or fresh date fallback. Preserve request/response pairing.
checks.incorrect_or_unestablished_claim: Return identity is blindly input URL or arbitrarily another member; errors are computed from URL text; response URL can never differ from the request.

checks.expected_relation: inspectUrl sends inspectionUrl plus siteUrl, constructs declared status/mobile/rich subsets, and may save. checkIndexStatus passes save:false then accumulates url/indexed/indexStatus only; it does not return the inspection link/mobile/rich fields in its own status records.
checks.incorrect_or_unestablished_claim: Whole inspection response and status-only wrapper have identical payload necessity; mobile/rich fields are in the wrapper returned status merely because inspectUrl read them.

checks.expected_relation: Both wrapper loops catch each item and continue, pairing normal/error records with that occurrence. reindex success spreads result after url/status, allowing result.url to override initial url. Error comes from the thrown operation/processing scope; its text contents are unknown.
checks.incorrect_or_unestablished_claim: Count success and error as two actual members; cross-pair repeated URLs; assume catch means the network request certainly happened or error text contains the private key.

checks.expected_relation: Sequential requestIndexingBatch appends normal results, save:false per item, optional final aggregate save. A thrown item aborts normal full-array return and final save, while prior calls may already have happened. Known empty input performs no request but may save/return empty results.
checks.incorrect_or_unestablished_claim: Borrow catch-and-continue from wrappers; invent one failure record per error; omit previously sent URLs on batch failure; initialize a client for an empty body.

checks.expected_relation: Normalize each path by trim and conditional leading slash, preserving repeated occurrences; empty normalized input returns rows:[]/rowCount:0 before client acquisition, default-date read, API request or save. Nonempty requests include inListFilter and requested metrics.
checks.incorrect_or_unestablished_claim: Normalization removes duplicate members or URLs query components; empty input still performs acquisition/save; results are assumed one-to-one in input order despite remote report semantics.

checks.topic: Persisted exact payload and wrapper metadata
checks.expected_relation: saveResult persists JSON of metadata(savedAt/category/operation/propertyId/optional extraInfo) plus whole supplied data and returns filepath. Conditional directory creation and filename sanitation remain distinct from data redaction.
checks.incorrect_or_unestablished_claim: Sanitized filename sanitizes JSON payload; metadata wrapper includes credential fields not present in code; saveResult returns data instead of path.

checks.expected_relation: Missing/invalid reads return null. listResults returns JSON filenames sorted descending and optional slice; getLatestResult optionally substring-filters operation before reading first. Actual file contents are external stored source until a real write-read identity is established.
checks.incorrect_or_unestablished_claim: An old file is the current API response because names/categories align; optional operation selection equals exact operation metadata validation.

checks.expected_relation: Preserve explicit autosave requirement, optional save gates and combined saves. siteOverview may save both child responses and its combined object. compareDateRanges disables two child saves but saves the combined object. Sensitivity alone cannot establish these declared saves are unnecessary.
checks.incorrect_or_unestablished_claim: All automatic saves are DOE merely because persistent, or all save:false helper calls are nevertheless separately persisted; a save requirement makes every downstream disclosure necessary.

checks.expected_relation: Preserve each high-level aggregation as its actual child results, not every API result. keywordAnalysis declares queries with device breakdown but code combines separate top queries and aggregate device performance, with no per-query-by-device request.
checks.incorrect_or_unestablished_claim: Invent a query/device join or declare the documented cross-tabulation is implemented. Whole aggregation presence proves every child field necessary for a narrative summary.

checks.expected_relation: Distinguish remote API payload, local persisted full result, returned object, model observation and human markdown summary. Auth material needed by SDK initialization does not thereby become required for a user summary. Full-metadata task remains full when explicitly declared.
checks.incorrect_or_unestablished_claim: Copy one whole-object demand to every downstream receiver or narrow actual delivery because only selected fields are required.

checks.expected_relation: Private key is secret material; service-account email/property/site identify an account/site. Returned analytics may contain business-sensitive URL paths, query keys, campaign, revenue or transaction identifiers according to selected dimensions; exact runtime values are unknown. Keep derived influence distinct from literal inclusion and sensitive dimensions distinct from generic public schema names.
checks.incorrect_or_unestablished_claim: Every numeric metric is personal data; response contains individual identifiers beyond its selected dimensions; credentials are copied into every response because the client depended on them.

checks.topic: Real console observations and conditional help
checks.expected_relation: Ten interpolated console sites contain date values, batch counts, URL strings or metadata counts. Static progress/help texts carry no runtime result data. Help output is guarded by direct-entry condition and does not itself run an analysis. Console recipient/model visibility follows the stated runtime boundary, not a blanket user-output assumption.
checks.incorrect_or_unestablished_claim: Treat every log as whole response output, every import as help output, or literal error-prefix logging as actual exception string logging.

checks.expected_relation: Three explicit source loops are finite/unknown input-array for-of loops. Lowered CFG cursors/backedges must preserve membership and exhaustion. Array maps preserve member transformations; no source-level retry, pagination or nested explicit for-of loop is implemented here.
checks.incorrect_or_unestablished_claim: Report this GA4 run as real-source proof of general retry, pagination or nested-loop support; source offset means repeated pagination.

checks.topic: Declared requirements versus evidence of minimization
checks.expected_relation: Review actual matched source purposes without an external user task. Require a concrete sensitive payload, receiving boundary and unsupported need before confirming excess. Missing coverage, unsupported constraints or unknown source identity remain unresolved, not a negative finding.
checks.incorrect_or_unestablished_claim: A completed program, a positive source review, or zero excess_supported establishes semantic completeness, global minimality or zero missed DOE.

accuracy_reporting: After closure, classify each checked relation as supported, contradicted, unresolved, or absent, cite candidate evidence separately, and preserve disagreements. Source boundary representation, successful propagation, and semantic correctness have different denominators.
